value.rationale: The Desargues graph is the canonical nonplanar cubic inclusion graph H(5,2) and a bipartite double-cover counterpart to the Petersen graph. Its central complement involution has mathematically distinguished geometric meaning. Splitting the 35-dimensional degree-two homology into specifically named Specht constituents with parity 15+20 identifies structure invisible in ordinary Betti ranks, and it predicts sharply different homology for the complement-only versus full symmetric quotients. The exact representation is a natural missing invariant of a highly symmetric incidence graph, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
